questions.q: Who first described the data mesh architecture, per this lesson?
options: Zhamak Dehghani, in a 2019 article later developed into a 2022 book
An anonymous open-source collective
A standards body (ISO or NIST)
DAMA International, as part of DMBOK
questions.explain: The lesson attributes data mesh to Zhamak Dehghani's 2019 article and her 2022 book, 'Data Mesh: Delivering Data-Driven Value at Scale.'

questions.q: What are the four principles data mesh is built on, per this lesson?
options: Domain-oriented ownership, data as a product, self-serve infrastructure platform, and federated computational governance
Centralization, standardization, automation, and auditing
Speed, cost, security, and compliance
Extraction, transformation, loading, and reporting
questions.explain: The four stated principles are domain ownership, data as a product, a self-serve platform, and federated computational governance.

questions.q: Per this lesson, who sits on the governing body in 'federated computational governance'?
options: A federation of domain representatives, together with the platform team
A single central executive with unilateral authority
External auditors only, with no internal staff
No one — governance happens with no human involvement at all
questions.explain: The lesson states governance is done by domain representatives themselves, together with the platform team — not an outside central authority.

questions.q: What makes governance 'computational' in data mesh's federated computational governance, per this lesson?
options: Agreed-upon global rules are embedded as automated checks directly in the self-serve platform, rather than enforced by manual review
All governance decisions are made by a random number generator
It means the rules are written only in mathematical notation
It refers only to the storage cost of running the platform
questions.explain: The lesson explains 'computational' means the rules are enforced automatically by the platform, not caught later by a human reviewer.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say data mesh is the most architecturally demanding of the four models in this chapter?
options: It requires real platform-engineering investment (a self-serve platform and defined product interfaces) before the governance model can function at all
It requires no infrastructure investment of any kind
It is identical in requirements to decentralized governance
It can be implemented with a single spreadsheet
questions.explain: The lesson states mesh needs a substantial self-serve platform and defined data-product interfaces before computational governance can even function.
